walkthrough.title: One record through a queue-driven stage

steps.title: A clock goes off, and a container is born
steps.body:
Every five minutes a cron expression fires. The platform creates an **execution**, and that execution starts a **replica** — a fresh container with nothing in memory.

It fetches the source and finds one new record. Nothing downstream knows yet.

notes.title: Job, execution, replica
notes.body: The job is the definition. An execution is one run. A replica is the container that run starts.

steps.title: It knocks on a queue and walks away
steps.body:
The producer sends **one message** to the stage queue. The message does not carry the record — only that work exists. The data stays in the store.

Then the producer exits.

notes.title: Queue, message, topic
notes.body: A queue is the mailbox, a message is one letter in it. A topic would photocopy the letter to many subscribers; this chain uses none.

steps.title: Something has to be looking
steps.body: A visible message summons nobody. The queue is a passive mailbox. Every thirty seconds the scaler asks how many messages are visible, hears `1`, and asks the platform for a worker execution.

steps.title: The store says what the work actually is
steps.body:
The worker takes the message with a **peek-lock** — hidden from everyone else for five minutes, not deleted. Then it asks the store to claim a batch in a single indivisible step.

That atomic claim, not the queue, is what makes double processing impossible.

notes.title: Why the message stays empty
notes.body: The store is the single source of truth and the message is only a nudge, so the two can never disagree.

steps.title: Do the work, then close the loop
steps.body:
The worker writes its result and then tells the queue **Complete()** — done, delete it. This is the first moment the message is truly removed rather than hidden.

Finishing the work is not enough; until the queue is told, it will hand the message to someone else in five minutes.

notes.title: Three endings
notes.body: Complete deletes it. Abandon puts it back for a retry. Dead-letter parks it for a human after the last attempt.

steps.title: Knock the next door, then disappear
steps.body:
The same move, one door along: a new message to the next stage, and the worker exits. The scaler sees an empty queue and scales back to zero.

Nothing is running anywhere.

cards.title: What the store supplies
items: The atomic claim makes double work impossible
The message never carries the record
